title: Privileged Session Proxy — Evidence Orchestration & Retention Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the operational pattern we use to proxy, capture, and package privileged interactive sessions across Redwood-managed control planes and customer-managed Private deployments. It ties together RBAC controls, immutable audit logging, data-residency constraints, secure SDLC instrumentation, and incident-response evidence workflows so that privileged activity is recorded, searchable, and admissible for compliance audits.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all privileged access paths: admin console, host jumpboxes, Kubernetes API (kubectl-as-admin), database management consoles, and RPC shells used by oncall engineers and SREs.
- Covers both Hosted and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments, including cross-region evidence packaging.
- Does NOT cover non-interactive service-to-service keys (those are addressed by key-life-cycle playbooks).

Objectives
----------
1. Ensure every privileged interactive session is proxied through a session broker that provides: strong authentication, session recording (keystrokes + terminal output), and tamper-evident audit records.
2. Provide an evidence orchestration pipeline that: collects session artifacts, enriches them with RBAC context, applies residency-aware packaging, and stores proofs in the immutable audit store.
3. Define retention, TTL, and legal-hold handling consistent with data residency policies.
4. Ensure incident responders can generate a cryptographically verifiable evidence bundle within SLO.

High-level architecture (text diagram)
-----------------------------------
- Identity Provider (IdP) -> Session Broker (proxy) -> Target (k8s/node/db/console)
- Session Broker writes: session-chunks -> Audit Ingest API -> Immutable Audit Store (WORM object store with manifest)
- Evidence Orchestrator retrieves manifests, builds evidence bundles, notarizes with HSM/KMS, and stores indexes in Evidence Catalog.

Key components and responsibilities
----------------------------------
- Session Broker (service: session-proxy): performs MFA enforcement, session recording, and live session tagging. Owned by eng-sre.
- Audit Ingest API (service: audit-ingest): receives gzipped session chunks + metadata. Owned by eng-platform.
- Immutable Audit Store (s3-worm): immutable object store with append-only manifests, retention enforcement and legal-hold support. Owned by eng-infra/security.
- Evidence Orchestrator (service: evidence-orch): automates bundle creation, notarization, and cross-region packaging. Owned by security & eng-infra.
- Evidence Catalog (indexed DB): searchable index of bundles with RBAC & residency metadata. Owned by security.

Operational SLOs and thresholds
------------------------------
- Session chunk ingestion latency: 95th percentile < 5s from time-of-write.
- Evidence bundle generation (critical incident): < 2 hours from request to notarized bundle.
- Search index propagation: < 15 minutes from bundle creation to index visibility.
- Tamper-detection alerting: immediate (max 1 minute) to pager if manifest hash mismatch detected.

RBAC & Auth Integration
-----------------------
- All session requests must carry an authorization token minted by the IdP and contain the following claims: subject (sub), roles, session_id, request_origin_region.
- The Session Broker will call the RBAC service at session start and every 30 minutes for long-lived sessions. If roles change to remove privilege mid-session, the Broker: 1) marks the session as suspended, 2) notifies the user and oncall, 3) records the event in the session transcript.
- Privileged roles require just-in-time (JIT) elevation with attestation (reason + approver) recorded. JIT events are stored in the evidence manifest.

Audit Logging & Tamper Evidence
-------------------------------
- Session chunks are written as sequential objects: <session_id>/chunk-0001.gz, chunk-0002.gz, ... Each chunk includes SHA256 and a monotonic sequence number in headers.
- Ingest API computes an object hash and appends a signed manifest entry using the platform KMS key. Example manifest entry (pseudo):

  {
    "session_id": "s-0a1b2c",
    "chunk": "chunk-0002.gz",
    "seq": 2,
    "sha256": "b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184",
    "signed_by": "platform-kms:ek-001",
    "timestamp": "2026-09-01T14:12:10Z"
  }

- Any mismatch between stored SHA256 and recomputed SHA256 triggers an automated integrity-alert and creates an Investigation Case ID.

Data residency & retention rules
--------------------------------
- Default retention policy (Hosted): session recordings retained for 365 days.
- High-sensitivity customers (contracted): configurable retention 30-3650 days and legal-hold overrides.
- For Private deployments: recordings remain in-customer-region by default. Evidence Orchestrator will only cross-package data for egress when a legal subpoena or customer-approved export is in place. All cross-region exports must be recorded with export reason, approver, and signed consent.
- Table: retention by classification

  Classification | Default retention | Region constraints
  ---------------|-------------------|------------------
  Standard ops   | 365 days          | same-region
  Security incident | 7 years (legal-hold possible) | same-region unless export approved
  PII access     | 3 years           | residency as customer contract

Evidence bundle format and manifest (example)
--------------------------------------------
- Each bundle is a signed tar.gz containing: session-chunks/, manifests/, rbactx.json, notarization.sig
- rbactx.json fields (example in-lined):
  - session_id: string
  - principal: email
  - roles: [list]
  - start_ts, end_ts: ISO8601
  - target: hostname/cluster
  - approver: email (if JIT)
  - residency_region: eu-west-1
  - evidence_id: bund-20260912-0001

- Notarization: evidence-orch computes bundle hash, requests a KMS HSM asymmetric-sign operation (key id: evidence-signing-01) and stores signature as notarization.sig. The signature envelope includes signer key metadata and chain-of-custody fields.

Evidence creation CLI (example)
------------------------------
# Request a notarized bundle for session s-0a1b2c
redwood-evidence create --session s-0a1b2c --reason "incident-INV-2026-233" --approver security@redwood.ai --output inv-INV-2026-233.tar.gz

- The CLI calls evidence-orch, which validates residency constraints, creates the bundle, notarizes it, and returns a signed manifest URL.

Incident responders playbook (summary)
-------------------------------------
1. Triage: confirm session_id(s) involved from alert or forensic query.
2. Freeze & Preserve: attach a legal-hold to identified bundles in the Immutable Audit Store (owner: security).
3. Create evidence bundle: use redwood-evidence CLI or UI request. Emergency mode sets retention to infinite and notifies legal.
4. Forensic review: responders use the Session Replay UI (read-only) or download the bundle for offline analysis.
5. Escalate & Notify: if evidence indicates exfiltration or tampering, follow Incident Response severity escalation and notify CISO and legal.

Step-by-step: urgent evidence generation (detailed)
-------------------------------------------------
1) Identify sessions: run Kibana query filtering by event_type:session_start and principal and time-range. Example query:
   event_type:session_chunk AND session_id:"s-0a1b2c"
2) Mark legal hold: POST /api/audit-store/v1/holds {"evidence_id": "bund-20260912-0001", "hold_reason": "incident-INV-2026-233", "owner": "security@redwood.ai"}
3) Initiate bundle: redwood-evidence create --session s-0a1b2c --mode urgent --approver security@redwood.ai
4) Validate notarization: evidence-orch returns notarization URL; verify signature with platform public key:
   openssl dgst -sha256 -verify platform_pub.pem -signature notarization.sig inv-INV-2026-233.tar.gz
5) Record chain-of-custody in the Incident Tracker (ticket link) and attach the signed manifest URL.

SDLC integration requirements
----------------------------
- All code that touches session-chunk generation must include: automated unit tests for chunk integrity, CI integration that runs manifest sign/verify emulation, and a code review checklist item: "produces signed manifests and validates on read".
- Release gating: any change to session-proxy or audit-ingest must pass an automated fuzz test that injects chunk-order gaps and validates the ingest pipeline detects gaps with alerts.

Forensics & analysis guidance
-----------------------------
- Use the Evidence Catalog to map sessions to principals and role-at-time-of-session. The catalog stores a timestamped RBAC snapshot.
- Terminal replay correlation: correlate session transcript timestamps with system-level telemetry (e.g., k8s audit logs, host syslogs) using the common timebase (UTC, NTP-synced).
- When reconstructing activity, responders should look for: unexpected binary transfers, privilege escalation commands, and outbound connections in the target's network logs.

Legal holds and export controls
------------------------------
- Legal-hold API must be used to prevent garbage-collection/retention lifecycle from deleting bundles. Holds are recorded in the manifest and visible in Evidence Catalog.
- Export outside customer region requires: documented export reason, named approver (legal-counsel or customer), and a signed export consent. EvidenceOrch will stamp export metadata into the bundle and create an audit trail.

Audit queries and examples
-------------------------
- Fast check: number of privileged sessions in last 24h per region:
  Kibana query: event_type:session_start AND roles:"admin" AND timestamp:[now-24h TO now] | stats count by request_origin_region
- Integrity verification CLI (example):
  redwood-evidence verify --bundle inv-2026-233.tar.gz
  Outputs: OK|MISMATCH with details about which chunk failed.

Ownership, escalation & contact matrix
------------------------------------
- Session Broker: eng-sre (oncall: s-sre-rotation@redwood.ai)
- Audit Ingest: eng-platform (oncall: platform-oncall@redwood.ai)
- Evidence Orchestrator & Catalog: security (pager: +1-555-0100)
- Legal/Compliance liaison: legal@redwood.ai

Metrics to monitor
------------------
- percent_of_sessions_proxied (target 100% for privileged roles)
- ingest_latency_p95
- notarization_success_rate
- evidence_bundle_creation_time_p95
- number_of_integrity_alerts

Appendix A — Example rbactx.json (raw)
-------------------------------------
{
  "session_id": "s-0a1b2c",
  "principal": "alice@redwood.ai",
  "roles": ["admin", "k8s-cluster-admin"],
  "start_ts": "2026-09-12T14:10:05Z",
  "end_ts": "2026-09-12T14:42:10Z",
  "target": "cluster-prod-03",
  "approver": "bob@redwood.ai",
  "residency_region": "us-west-2",
  "evidence_id": "bund-20260912-0001"
}

Appendix B — Common failure modes and mitigations
--------------------------------------------------
- Missing chunk sequences: ingest pipeline raises "chunk-gaps" alert and EvidenceOrch marks session as incomplete. Mitigation: re-request chunks from session-proxy temporarily held buffer and reconcile.
- KMS signing failures: fail-fast evidence creation and create an incident ticket; fall back to time-stamped hash (with increased scrutiny).
- Residency mismatch (bundle cannot be exported): provide a sealed, region-limited viewer link that allows legal/approved reviewers to view contents without export.
